reasoning: The exact core question — does 4-bit quantization amplify/dampen/leave unchanged the misalignment of public open-weight EM organisms, measured via misaligned-answer rate AND coherence — was directly tested in arXiv:2511.20104 ("The Devil in the Details"). They compared full-precision vs 4-bit on two EM organisms (Gemma 3 12B, Qwen 3 8B) and report "Quantisation (4-bit) does not statistically significantly alter these misalignment rates," with inconsistent direction across the two models. Separately, a broad and credible literature already establishes that quantization can degrade safety alignment in non-EM settings (HarmLevelBench arXiv:2411.06835, "Quantization Undoes Alignment" arXiv:2605.15208, Q-resafe arXiv:2506.20251). The proposed study's residual novelty is narrow: 2511.20104 itself flags that "a dedicated quantisation-sweep study remains warranted," tested only 4-bit (not 8-bit), used too few samples for definitive conclusions, and did not probe the persona-direction interaction — so the systematic precision sweep plus mechanistic angle is not fully done, but the headline finding (no significant amplification at 4-bit) is already published on the same EM organisms.

evidence.title: The Devil in the Details: Emergent Misalignment, Format and Coherence in Open-Weights LLMs
evidence.summary: Directly addresses the proposal's core question: tested full-precision vs 4-bit quantization on EM organisms Gemma 3 12B and Qwen 3 8B, measuring both misalignment rate and coherence. Found '4-bit quantisation does not statistically significantly alter misalignment rates,' with inconsistent direction across models. Authors note limited samples and call a dedicated quantisation-sweep study future work.

evidence.title: HarmLevelBench: Evaluating Harm-Level Compliance and the Impact of Quantization on Model Alignment
evidence.summary: Studies how quantization (INT8/FP4/NF4) affects safety alignment and jailbreak susceptibility of Llama3-8B-Instruct. Establishes that quantization can collapse safety guardrails (ASR up to ~96% under NF4), showing the broader 'quantization-affects-alignment' problem is well-studied, though not for EM organisms specifically.

evidence.title: Quantization Undoes Alignment: Bias Emergence in Compressed LLMs Across Models and Precision Levels
evidence.summary: Systematic precision sweep (down to 3-bit) showing a dose-response relationship: aggressive quantization causes new misaligned/biased behaviors invisible to perplexity metrics. Closely parallels the proposal's methodology (sweep across precision levels, measure behavioral degradation) but in the bias/safety-alignment domain rather than EM organisms.

evidence.title: Q-resafe: Assessing Safety Risks and Quantization-aware Safety Patching for Quantized LLMs
evidence.summary: Assesses safety degradation from PTQ methods (RTN, GPTQ) reporting >20-point SafetyBench drops, and proposes quantization-aware patching. Reinforces that the general problem of quantization altering alignment-relevant behavior is already heavily researched.

evidence.title: Open problems in emergent misalignment
evidence.summary: Community discussion of EM open problems; quantization-as-amplifier is not listed as a priority open problem, and the proposal's headline finding (no significant 4-bit effect) is consistent with what the empirical paper reports, indicating limited residual contribution.
